findings.description: The bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects (including the uploaded vendor roster) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS encryption.

findings.issue_category: no explicit ACL or public access block
findings.description: No acl is set and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, leaving the bucket without explicit protection against public ACLs or bucket policies that would expose report data.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy is true, so objects can be overwritten or deleted irrecoverably, destroying evidence and data integrity.
No logging block is configured, so unauthorized access to the report data cannot be detected or investigated.
The ledger export bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so sensitive financial export data is stored unencrypted with no KMS key control.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so ledger export objects can be silently overwritten or deleted with no recovery path.
No server access logging is configured for this financial data bucket, preventing detection of unauthorized reads or exfiltration.
The model artifacts bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, so artifacts are not encrypted with a managed KMS key at rest.
The runbooks bucket has no server-side encryption configured; operational runbooks frequently contain hostnames, procedures and secrets that would be stored in plaintext.
No logging block is defined, so access to sensitive operational documentation is not auditable.

The audit/log-delivery bucket itself has no access logging or object-lock/MFA-delete protection, and force_destroy is true, so an attacker with bucket access could tamper with or destroy the audit trail.
A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing third-party PII/contact data) is uploaded with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id specified into a bucket that also lacks default encryption.
